_doc: Session 15 (Sérgio Round 24), restructured Session 27 (R28-0c, D14/D15): THREE INTIMATE ROOMS THAT AGE, one shell. r1 = reinterp E1 (witness furniture out; spine door + record terminal). r2 = E2, HOMECOMING (D15): Daniel comes back to the SAME closed Room 1, aged — the walls do NOT open here (Sérgio: "at Era 2 the room ages but stays CLOSED"). r3 = T2 "the room OPENS, it does not explode" (moved from T1/E2): Room 1 (Daniel, gay) keeps its EXACT E1 walls/desk/front-wall distance; its side walls become DOORWAYS revealing Room 2 (west/Vera, lesbian) and Room 3 (east/Maya, trans) — two adjacent intimate bedrooms at the SAME scale, axis-aligned (90° only), each read at E1 desk-intimacy when the camera dollies in — AND Room 1 closes (Daniel "transferred") in the same state. r4 = E4: the focus is Room 3 (Maya = the trans room evolved — NOT a separate desk; ◆N3 TURN retargets here); windows go dark for good. Rooms built from ONE local bedroom template (scratchpad/gen_rooms.mjs) placed per room — bed on a side wall, door away from the bed, clean CRT. COLOR LAW: every hex from era1.json family.

cdStack._doc: Session 49 logged this and left it (its own finding-2 note, verbatim): 'cdStack (era1.json, pos y0.71 / half-height 0.07) still sits at the OLD box-shelf height and is now ~12cm sunk into the bookcase model's shelf — the same class of bug as the tapes' y0.646.' Session 54 fixes it: cdStack's base (0.71-0.07=0.64) targeted the OLD box shelfBoard1's top; the REAL bookcaseModel's bottom shelf surface is y0.76 (the same shared shelf boombox/tapeA/tapeB/mixtape already measure against — one shelf run, several props). New y0.83 puts cdStack's base back at 0.76, +0.12 from the old 0.71, matching the ~12cm S49 estimated by eye. teddyBox sits on the same old shelfBoard1 baseline and had the identical sink — flagged then, fixed now below (Session 55), since this session is already re-measuring this exact shelf. Session 55 ALSO moved x/z (1.98,0.9 → 2.02,0.62): its old z0.9 sat squarely in the middle of the three shelf tapes' new z-run (0.87-1.07 — the boombox's own Session 55 re-rotation widened its footprint and pushed the tapes into that space, see tapeA's _doc), and cdStack's box very nearly fully occluded tapeA from the seat (confirmed live: toggling cdStack.enabled off/on in-browser made tapeA go from invisible to visible). The shelf run only has ~0.3m free after the boombox — not enough for 3 legible tapes AND a 0.12m cdStack side by side — so cdStack moves to a second depth track instead, tucked behind the boombox (x2.02, near the bookcase's own back wall at x2.098, z0.62 matching the boombox's own z-centre) rather than competing for the same front row. rainbowDuck._doc: Session 84: measured against the rendered bookcaseOpen.glb, not the retired box shelf. era1.json put the duck base at y1.560, which was the OLD shelfBoard3 top; the real model's top board spans y1.558–1.615, so that base sat 5.5 cm inside the board. Its z footprint was 0.33–0.43 against the model's 0.37 front edge, overhanging by 4 cm; that partial footprint is also why room-audit could not classify the bookcase AABB as support and reported the floor instead. y1.655 puts the 0.04 m half-height exactly on y1.615; z0.50 keeps the full 0.10 m depth inside the shelf with 8 cm of front margin. From the Room-1 seat it shares teddyBox's bearing: 84.2° right of the authored forward direction, one deliberate right turn. Session 86: y1.655 → 1.712, and this is the third session to touch it because the first two MEASURED and never LOOKED. Disabling the duck live, from the Room-1 seat at its own bearing, changed nothing at all on screen — it was not merely hard to see, it was invisible. The live bookcaseOpen.glb AABB tops out at y1.672, not the y1.615 S84 measured, so a 0.08 m duck based at 1.615 was buried 5.7 cm inside the top board with 2.3 cm showing behind the board's own front lip. 1.712 puts the 0.04 m half-height exactly on the real 1.672 surface. Verified by eye at the seat, at pitch 0 and pitched up, before and after. S90: `model: rubberDuck` added — the actual fix for the finding above ('it was never a duck'), not a fourth coordinate pass. This flips the placement convention: a BOX prop's `pos.y` is its CENTRE (era1.json's own doc, 'pos = center of the box'), so S86's 1.712 was built as 1.672 (the shelf surface) + 0.04 (half the box's own height). A MODEL prop's `pos.y` is instead the world height of the model's OWN measured base (`assets.ts spawnModel`: the wrapper is placed at `pos`, and the model is pre-shifted by `-baseY*scale` so its native base lands at the wrapper's local origin) — `rubberDuck`'s manifest entry (data/room/models.json) has `baseY: 0` (already resting on its own base), so feeding it the old box-centre y1.712 would float the duck 4cm above the real shelf. y1.712 → 1.672, putting the model's own base exactly on the live-measured shelf surface, no half-height math left to do. Verified live: camera at the Room-1 seat, turned to the duck's own ~84° bearing, screenshotted — a real duck, resting on the shelf board with no gap and no overhang.

mixtape._doc: Session 49 (finding 2): moved CLEAR of the cassette player and onto its shelf surface (full story on tapeA's own _doc below). Session 54: gave it `model: cassetteTape` too — a FIRST for a `props` override (every other model prop up to now was introduced via `add`, since Session 32's boombox override silently dropped `model`). Fixed properly this time, at the root: clusterMorph.ts's `foldTargets` now also copies `o.model` out of a `props` override, and `ClusterMorph.snapTo` re-spawns an EXISTING baseline id as the real mesh the first time its fold asks for one (mixtape was spawned as a box by era1room.ts's initial pass, long before this fold ever runs, so `spawnTarget`'s normal 'first spawn places itself' path never sees it). Kept as an override rather than a remove+add (the tapeA/tapeB pattern) on purpose: mixtape is both a belongings.json-eligible KEEPSAKE (its id must stay literally 'mixtape' for the ledger/kept-glow/click geometry) and a prop that RELOCATES at r3 (see that state's own props.mixtape) — a remove+add-new-id there would have raced the belongings 'kept freeze' (which re-asserts the r1 target under the ORIGINAL id) into showing two tapes at once, and tools/check-rooms.mjs's double-add check rejects remove+add of the SAME id within one state outright. `applyTarget`'s model branch now also re-applies position on every fold (previously model props were position-frozen after spawn), which is what lets r3's override actually move it. Session 55: `model` swapped `cassetteTape`→`cassetteTapeShelf` (data/room/models.json) — standing upright instead of lying flat, so it reads as a thing to pick up rather than a chip of debris. `pos` ALSO moved this round (x1.74→1.86, z1.09→1.07): the boombox's own Session 55 re-rotation changed its footprint from a thin vertical tower (x~1.78-1.94, barely into the shelf's z-run) to a wide landscape box (same x-depth, but z0.42-0.82) — at the tapes' old x1.74 they sat shallower than (visually 'in front of') the now-much-wider boombox instead of beside it; matching x1.86 puts every shelf object at the same depth, and mixtape's z nudges from 1.09 to 1.07 to keep clear of tapeB's new z0.97 slot (see tapeA/tapeB's own _doc for the full re-layout). Session 56: y0.766→0.709 — see boomboxModel's _doc, this whole shelf's `y0.76` was measured against the wrong surface; the real one is 0.057 lower. `yaw: 8` added too (same as tapeA/tapeB — a small turn toward the seat, see tapeA's _doc), which needed `clusterMorph.ts`'s `foldTargets` to also copy `yaw` out of a `props` override — the same silent-drop gap `model` had until Session 55, this time for a different field.

Session 49 (finding 2): the REAL cassette player, finally on the shelf. Session 32 tried to do this by putting `model: cassettePlayer` on an r1 OVERRIDE of the box-built `boombox` prop — but clusterMorph.ts's fold only copies color/pos/size out of `props` overrides, so the key was silently dropped and the shelf kept showing an anonymous dark box (the 418KB GLB was downloaded and never used). Overrides still cannot introduce a model; an ADD can (foldTargets passes def.model, and spawnTarget spawns it), which is how deskModel/chairModel/bookcaseModel already work. So the four box props are removed above and this replaces them. pos/size are Session 32's own measured values, kept verbatim: centered in the bookcase's rendered depth (x:[1.623,2.098]) with clearance on both shelf edges; `size` remains the fallback-box geometry if the GLB ever fails to load. Session 56: y0.76→0.703 — every shelf-1 prop's `y0.76` back to Session 32 turns out to have been measuring against the WRONG surface. Extracted the real bookcaseOpen.glb's own shelf-board vertices directly (`mesh.getPositions()` transformed by the entity's world matrix, bucketed by Y — no 3D viewer, same live-measurement discipline this pipeline has always used, just a level deeper than an AABB this time): the boards sit at y[0.190,0.247], [0.646,0.703], [1.102,1.159], [1.558,1.615] — four boards, five compartments. Cross-checked against book1 (era1.json, undisputed correct placement for 17+ sessions): its base is 1.10, matching board 3's top (1.102) almost exactly, confirming the method. The boombox/tapes/cdStack/teddyBox compartment is the one BELOW that (bounded by the board at 0.646-0.703), so its floor is 0.703, not 0.76 — every prop on this shelf was resting 5.7cm above its actual surface the whole time, which finally read as visibly wrong (Sérgio: 'the boombax is too up', 'a floating yellow tape') once the boombox stopped being a thin tower and started reading as a real object.

Session 74 (the E4 room pass, item 3 in scope: 'all the rooms built have still a lot of logistics and object errors' — S71's own P6 named this and left it: 'Room 1's curtains hang from nothing — Rooms 2 and 3 have a curtRod prop and Room 1 does not.' era1.json itself stays byte-identical to the shipped baseline (assets/LICENSES.md), so the fix lands here in r1 rather than on the baseline curtainLeft/curtainRight props themselves. Spans both curtains (x -1.50 to -0.40, matching e_curtRod/w_curtRod's own span logic) just above their authored top (curtainLeft/Right pos.y 1.5 + half-height 0.55 = 2.05), same brown as the side rooms' rods and the shelf/desk timber already in this room. FLOATING → held (room-audit.mjs's 'hangs' rule: a prop whose base sits within 0.03 m of another prop's underside).

r2._docS86: ⚑ Session 86 — E2 WAS STILL WEARING E1'S CLOTHES. Sérgio, playing the deployed build: "The pamphlet is still on the desk; the tape is still on the shelf. Era 2 should not be wearing Era 1's props." He was right on both counts, and the r2 fold was the thinnest in the file: it retired the boombox, tapeA/tapeB and their docked twins, and the moon, and nothing else — six years of this room's life were one recoloured window pane. Everything added below is an object that dates itself to 1997 and that a returning adult would not still have out. THE KIT (kitBrochure + its two folds, the cover band/title/motif, the three text blocks, the pocket flap and the floppy with its shutter and label) is the Family Design Solutions sales packet: its floppy has already been put into a machine that has since been updated twice, and the brochure lying open on the desk in 2003 reads as a set-dressing oversight rather than as a life. homeworkPile is a teenager's homework. sodaCan is the one judgement call in the list and is flagged for Sérgio — a can on a desk is not era-specific, and it is kept ONLY because removing it costs nothing to re-add if he disagrees. ⚑ NOT REMOVED, deliberately: mixtape (Tape C). It is belongings-eligible and the r3 fold relocates it onto bookcaseMoved with the duck and the teddy, so it is the one Era-1 object the piece has already decided survives — retiring it here would silently kill that payoff. FOR SÉRGIO: if the mixtape should also go, the honest place is the belongings beat (kept → frozen on the shelf; not kept → gone at r2), which would finally give that choice a visible consequence; it currently has none.

book1._doc: S89 — Sérgio: 'the shelf in Era 3 is still not against the wall, it should rotate so the wider side we can see it, like in Era-1, and the books are floating.' Both were the same root cause: bookcaseMoved (below) kept E1's yaw:90 (tuned for E1's wallEast, an X-facing wall) when it relocated to sit near wallSouth (a Z-facing wall) — wrong axis touching the wall, and its WIDE run facing along Z instead of toward the Room-2 seat. Rotating it 90° (yaw 90→0) swaps which world axis is 'along the shelf' and which is 'depth', so every prop riding on it needs the SAME 90° remap or it lands off the new shelf entirely — this is not a re-guess by eye, it is the old (x,z) offset from the bookcase's old centre rotated by the same -90° the bookcase itself just took (verified live: placing a test prop at the rotated offset landed it cleanly on the new shelf board, screenshot-confirmed, before this value was written here). Old offset from old centre (1.87,3.3) was (0.11,-0.2); rotated offset from the (pre-BOUNDS-fix) centre (1.87,3.44) was (0.2,0.11) → x2.07. The bookcase's own centre then moved 1.87→1.70 (its own _doc) to clear a BOUNDS overshoot the rotation introduced, carrying every rider the same -0.17 in x.

book2._doc: S89 — same remap as book1 (see its _doc), including the -0.17 x carry from the bookcase's own BOUNDS fix. Old offset from old centre (0.11,-0.1) → new offset from new centre (0.1,0.11) → x1.97 → x1.80.

book3._doc: S89 — same remap as book1 (see its _doc), including the -0.17 x carry. Old offset (0.11,-0.15) → new offset (0.15,0.11) → x2.02 → x1.85.

cdStack._doc: Session 71: this override said [1.98, 0.71, 3.45] — era1.json's ORIGINAL x and y plus 2.55 z. But r1 already corrects this prop to (2.02, 0.773) for two measured reasons (see r1's own _doc: the y put its base 0.063 m INSIDE the shelf board, and the x/z moved it off the tape run), and a later override replaces `pos` wholesale, so r3 silently reverted both. The fold's own hazard: an override further down the chain is not a delta, it is a replacement. Now r1's corrected position plus the shelf's +2.55 z. S89: bookcaseMoved's yaw 90→0 remap (see book1's _doc) applies here too, including its -0.17 x carry — old offset from old centre (0.15,-0.13) → new offset from new centre (0.13,0.15) → x2.00 → x1.83.

mixtape._doc: S89: bookcaseMoved's yaw 90→0 remap (see book1's _doc) applies here too, including its -0.17 x carry — old offset from old centre (0.11,0.08) → new offset from new centre (-0.08,0.11) → x1.79 → x1.62.

teddyBox._doc: Session 71: LEFT BEHIND. r3 moves the bookcase from z 0.75 to 3.3 and gives book1/book3/cdStack matching overrides — teddyBox and rainbowDuck never got one, so from E3 on they hung in mid-air in the middle of the vacated room (measured: 0.683 m and 1.540 m of clear air beneath them, tools/room-audit.mjs FLOATING). Both now carry the shelf's own +2.55 z, which preserves each prop's exact relationship to its compartment rather than re-placing it by eye. S89: bookcaseMoved's yaw 90→0 remap (see book1's _doc) applies here too, including its -0.17 x carry — old offset from old centre (0.11,0.1) → new offset from new centre (-0.1,0.11) → x1.77 → x1.60.

rainbowDuck._doc: Session 84: r3 must carry the corrected r1 shelf relationship, not the retired era1.json placement. Same x/y as r1 and the moved bookcase's exact +2.55 z. S89: bookcaseMoved's yaw 90→0 remap (see book1's _doc) applies here too, including its -0.17 x carry — old offset from old centre (0.11,-0.25) → new offset from new centre (0.25,0.11) → x2.12 → x1.95 (this also clears rainbowDuck's own BOUNDS overshoot, which was the other +x finding the rotation introduced). S90: y1.712→1.672, same box-centre→model-base fix as the r1 override above (see its _doc) — the shelf's own Y placement is unchanged by the x/z move or the yaw remap (a pure Y-axis rotation of the bookcase doesn't move its shelf boards' height), so the real surface is the same 1.672 measured at r1.

add._doc: ⚑ THE MESH GOES ON THE EXISTING PROP — 2026-08-21. Room 2 already had a w_keyboard box here and I added a SECOND declaration with the same id rather than editing this one. That is the third time in this build; a duplicate id does not error, the later declaration silently wins, and the earlier becomes invisible. CHECK FOR THE ID BEFORE ADDING A PROP. Kenney, CC0. Non-interactive and it must never be given a hit rect: the piece has no free-text input by law, so a pressable keyboard would promise something the work does not do.

⛑ THE INTAKE, TRANSFORMED — 2026-08-24, Sérgio's standing requirement: 'if the intake system is present on Era-1 it has to be TRANSFORMED into something new on Era-3.' It was not. S61 simply HID the record at E3 (witness-screen and terminalFrame both disabled) on the correct reasoning that 2016 is where the apparatus stopped being a place you go to — but hiding is not transforming, and a piece whose whole subject is an apparatus that changes form should never answer 'what happened to it' with 'it is gone'. ⛑ SO IT BECOMES INFRASTRUCTURE. In 1997 the record is a screen on the spine you can turn around and READ. In 2016 it is a cabinet standing in the same place with a light on it. The turn still lands on it. There is nothing to read. That is the era's thesis as an object rather than as an absence: the record did not stop existing, it stopped being addressed to her. Same spine, same bearing, same gesture, no text. ⛑ It exists at r3 only and is removed at r4, where the record migrates to Room 3's wall beside Maya and becomes readable again — the person and the record finally sharing a wall, which only lands if the record was somewhere else in between.

the one light on the cabinet, on the face turned into the room. It never blinks, never changes, and nothing in the piece remarks on it — it is on because the thing is running. Era 4's own mint, because this is what is arriving.

⛑ ROOM 2 HAD A MONITOR AND A KEYBOARD AND NOTHING DRIVING THEM — added 2026-08-24, Sérgio: 'Laptop? there is no laptop here...'. He was right twice: the code called Era 3's machine a LAPTOP everywhere (renamed to `workstation` this session, including the two player-visible strings) and the room had no tower, so a desk with a screen and a board on it read as a machine with no cause. It stands ON THE FLOOR at the far end of the desk. ⛑ I tried it on the desktop beside the monitor first, to get it inside the seat's 29.7° half-FOV, and it overlapped the monitor's own box by 104 mm on every arrangement that stayed in frame — the desk simply is not deep enough behind the panel. So it is where a tower actually goes, and it is seen on the entrance travelling and whenever she looks down, not from the chair at rest. That is a real limit and it is stated rather than hidden: if the room still does not read as a desktop, the next move is a second prop at eye level, not a bigger tower. ⛑ Beige, not black: this is a mid-2010s office tower issued to a worker, not a machine anybody chose.
the one light on it, on the face turned toward the chair. It never blinks, never signals anything, and nothing in the piece remarks on it — it is on because the machine is on.

⚑ ERA 3'S MONITOR IS NOW A MODEL — Kenney, CC0, 2026-08-21 (ERA3_BUILD_PLAN stage 2). It was four primitive boxes (body, screen, stand, foot) and is now one mesh that includes its own stand, so w_flatPanelStand and w_flatPanelFoot are removed with it. Net -2 props and -2 draw calls on an era that shares a budget with Rooms 1 and 3. ⚑ It SITS ON THE DESK (y 0.75, the desk top) rather than floating at the old body's y 1.1: the model's baseY is its bbox minimum, so it stands on its own foot the way a monitor does. Size is the model's LOCAL dims (0.51 wide x 0.38 tall x 0.135 deep) and yaw 90 turns the width onto z at render — authoring the size pre-rotated reports a +278%/-73% SCALE fault, which is how I first wrote it. w_flatPanelScreen and era3Devices' PLACEMENT.workstation plane move down to meet its face; if this prop is ever repositioned they must follow.

Session 74: z 0.7 → 0.61 (P1 in Session 71's log — the exact fix it proposed but did not apply). e_desk's own measured `modelScale` renders +50% deep on its local z, which put it 0.086 m inside e_bed; moving the desk clears it with a small margin instead of resizing the (correctly-measured) furniture. Every prop resting ON the desk (CRT, keyboard, mouse, folders) carries the same -0.09 z so the whole assembly stays together.

⛑ 2026-09-01: the CRT needed a shelf and the bookcase could not give it one. Its GLB is a single merged mesh whose compartments measure ~0.24m between planks — a 0.42m monitor straddles them, which is exactly what the first attempt rendered. Its TOP (y 1.672) does fit, but from the seat's eye at 1.16 that is ~31 degrees up, outside a 21 degree half-FOV: invisible at rest, and a remembrance nobody finds is not one. So: a plain plank on the north wall at 1.12, clear of the bookcase in x and the desk in z, putting the machine ~7 degrees above the eye — you turn, and it is there. ⛑ 1.25 -> 1.12 after looking: at 1.25 the monitor's top clipped the frame edge at rest. At 1.12 the whole machine spans roughly -0.4 to +14 degrees from the seated eye — entirely inside the half-FOV, nothing cropped.

⛑ 2026-09-01, Sérgio: 'maybe we can remove the book case and just keep some shelving just to change it up.' The bookcase went with it — a closed case in a room whose whole subject is a person's things being sorted and kept read as storage; open planks read as a life on display. This lower plank carries the books the case used to hold, at a height the seat meets rather than looks down into.

⛑ OFF THE DESK AND ONTO THE BOOKCASE, 2026-09-01. Sérgio: 'the computer doesnt make the most of sense to be here, maybe it could live on the shelf as a rememberance to the past, but it doesnt make sense to come from a wide computer to CRT.' He is right and the data agrees: Room 2's Era-3 machine is a 645x372mm WIDESCREEN, so the piece ran 1997 CRT -> 2016 widescreen -> 2026 CRT, which is time going backwards on the one surface a player reads eras from. ⛑ Room 3 is only ever seen in E4 (wallEast lifts at r4), so this desk WAS 2026's desk with a nineties monitor on it. ⛑ THIS SUPERSEDES S74's 'not deleted, not moved: the same machine across thirty years, finally off, still in the room' — the machine still is exactly that, and r4 still puts its screen out. It is simply kept rather than used: on top of the bookcase, turned to face the seat, the way people actually store the computer they cannot throw away. Placed against the measured model AABB (top y 1.672, x 4.052-4.527), not guessed. ⛑ ON THE SHELF, NOT ON TOP OF IT — measured, not guessed. The bookcase top is y 1.672, which from the seat's eye at 1.16 sits ~31 degrees up: outside a 21 degree half-FOV, so at rest you could not see it at all and a remembrance you cannot find is not one. The row-1 shelf puts it at eye level (pitch -2.6 degrees from the seat) where turning finds it. Its width is trimmed 0.50 -> 0.46 so it sits inside the case's measured 0.475 interior instead of clipping the side panels; the foot is dropped, because a monitor kept on a shelf is not standing on its tilt stand.

S89 — Sérgio, 2026-08-15: 'the shelf in Era 3 is still not against the wall, it should rotate so the wider side we can see it, like in Era-1, and the books are floating.' `yaw: 90` was carried over unchanged from E1's bookcaseModel (which correctly hugs wallEast, an X-facing wall, at x1.87 — the SAME x this prop kept). But r3 removes wallEast entirely (see this state's own `remove`) and this prop's own z-move (0.75→3.3) put it near wallSouth instead — a Z-facing wall — so yaw:90 was now presenting the shelf's NARROW depth face to wallSouth and its WIDE run parallel to it, i.e. sideways to the room, which reads as a thin floating plank from the Room-2 seat (verified live: at yaw90 near wallSouth the rendered world AABB is x[1.623,2.098] (0.475 wide) z[2.92,3.68] (0.76 wide) — the WIDE dimension was running along Z, away from the seat, not toward it). yaw:0 swaps that (live-verified world AABB at yaw0: x[1.49,2.25] (0.76 wide) z[3.072,3.547] (0.475 deep)) — matching E1's own relationship to ITS wall exactly, just rotated a quarter-turn to face a Z-wall instead of an X-wall. `pos.z` 3.3→3.44 seats the (now-correctly-oriented) back face flush against wallSouth (z3.72, thickness 0.04) with the same ~1.2cm clearance E1's copy keeps against wallEast, rather than floating 15cm short of it. `pos.x` 1.87→1.70: the quarter-turn also swapped which axis carries the WIDTH (0.76 m) — at yaw0 that's now x, and the unchanged x1.87 pushed the shelf 0.12 m past the room's own floor plate on +x (`tools/room-audit.mjs`'s BOUNDS check, floor x-range [-2.13,2.13]), a regression this same fix introduced and caught before commit. x1.70 (half-width 0.38) sits it at x[1.32,2.08], back inside the floor with room to spare. Every prop riding this shelf (book1/2/3, teddyBox, rainbowDuck, cdStack, mixtape) got the matching 90° offset remap AND this same x-shift — see book1's own _doc for the maths and the live verification.

⛑ MOVED AGAIN, 2026-08-24, and this time to be REACHABLE: from (-5.02, 1.16) to (-5.10, 0.95). Measured from the workstation seat, the phone's screen projected to (-230, 1214) on a 1280x900 viewport — off the left edge AND below the bottom — and looking down never recovered it, because at z 1.16 it sat 36.5° off the view axis against a 29.7° horizontal half-FOV. THE WHOLE ENDING OF ERA 3 IS ON THIS DEVICE. It is now 19.7° off axis and enters the frame from a -10° look. ⛑ KEEP THIS IN STEP with era3Devices' PLACEMENT.phone — the prop and its screen have now been separated twice, and both times Sérgio found it before a check did. ⚑ ERA 3'S PHONE — one mesh, ON THE DESK, 2026-08-21. It was a parts-built box on the nightstand at (-2.42, 0.51, -0.72). ⚑ The move is the era's thesis in a coordinate: the tablet lived across the room and was reached by a seat jump, and the phone is hers and stays within reach. The desk is where she is employed, the phone is where she is a person, both at arm's length — which is what makes ignoring it a real CHOICE rather than a walk she declines to take. Its two hand-built parts (body + earpiece) are gone; the mesh carries them. ⚑ A note for the next prop added here: I first declared a SECOND w_phoneDevice rather than editing this one, and a duplicate id does not error — the later declaration silently wins and the earlier becomes invisible. Check for the id first.

Session 74: an empty third shelf keeps a pencil tin rather than a third row of books — the point of a bookcase not entirely full of books (this is fog-tier per era1room.ts's classifyProp, the same recede-into-background treatment as homeworkPile).
Session 74 — the desk, in front of the keyboard (the free strip the headset's own fixtures will share at r4 — see that block's doc).
Session 74: the chair — same drape-over-the-back logic as w_cardigan (Session 66), a different garment and a different colour so the two rooms don't read as the same person twice.
Session 74: the bed — a second pillow toward the nightstand end, a folded throw at the foot.
Session 74: the nightstand top — a glass of water, an earbuds case, a small clock. The phone itself arrives at r4 (the era's device timeline, e_phoneBody/e_phoneCam below) on the same surface.
Session 74: floor-standing, near the window — same plant as Room 2's own (w_plant_pot/top), the one item deliberately shared rather than re-invented (a plant is not a personality trait).
Session 74: by the door — a life that goes outside this room. Not Vera's laundry basket: a backpack, a kicked-off pair of sneakers, keys dropped on the way in.

Session 74: the rug and the floor between the bed and the desk — a cushion to sit on the floor with, a book left open where she was reading, a water bottle, a small speaker (the same idea as Room 1's boombox and Room 2's radio, one generation newer).
Session 74: the bookcase's own top edge — a small framed photo (the same idea as w_frame, leaning against the case rather than hung, per the live measurement that showed w_frame does the same).

r3._docDeskCleared: ⛑ e_keyboard and e_mouse REMOVED 2026-09-01 with the CRT's move (Sérgio: 'we can[not] really see it with all the clutter here' — 'it' being the headset, the era's ONE interaction and until now the least legible object on the desk). They were that machine's peripherals; wired to nothing they are just clutter in front of the thing the era is actually about. What stays is hers and not the apparatus's: the folders, her glasses, and the headset on its dock.

e_crtScreen._doc: Session 74: THE CRT GOES DARK AND STAYS (build plan fixture list, item 3 — was blue, i.e. still reading as ON). #15151F is the same 'off' hex every other window/screen in this r4 block already goes to (windowPane/w_winPane/e_winPane above) — reused, not invented. This prop is spawned `emissive:true` (r3's own add), so an override here replaces its emissive colour directly (clusterMorph.applyTarget copies `color` straight onto the emissive channel for an emissive prop) — there is no separate 'off' switch in this data schema, so 'as dark as the rest of the dead glass in this room' is how off is expressed. Not deleted, not moved: the same machine across thirty years, finally off, still in the room.

add._doc: Session 74: THE PHONE GETS A REAL MODEL (fixture list item 4 — was a single untextured box; see w_phoneDevice's own _doc in r3 for why this is a primitive assembly rather than a GLB). Moved from the desk to the nightstand — bedside charging is the more honest place for it, and it frees the desk's front strip for the headset below, which the fixture list marks as the thing that actually needs to be within reach of the seat. Nothing in code keys off the literal id `e_phone` (checked: `app.ts`'s held-read list only covers Room 2's tablet/phone), so this rename is safe.

Session 74: THE HONEST DETAIL (fixture list — 'whatever she moves to put it on... one small honest detail; the body is in the room'). Her glasses, set down beside the stand — the ordinary human gesture of taking them off before the headset goes on.

⛑ THE REAL HEADSET (2026-09-01, Sérgio supplied the model). Replaces the five-box assembly this session spent three passes trying to make read as a headset — a shape problem that a shape solves. ⛑ z 0.30 IS KEPT: S76 measured the box at 33.9 degrees off the seat bearing against a 29.7 degree half-FOV, outside the frame, and 0.30 is that fix. PLACEMENT.visor's screen plane must stay in step with this prop or the visor detaches from itself. ⛑ 2026-09-01, LEFT AND BIGGER (Sérgio) — but left is BOUNDED, and the first attempt proved it. At z 0.16 the visor plane projected to (-44, 762) from the seat: off the left edge entirely, undoing the very fix S76 made when it measured the headset at 33.9 degrees off-bearing. Horizontal half-FOV here is ~28.6 degrees, so how far left this can go depends on how far BACK it sits: pushed to x 5.53 it can reach z 0.25 at ~24 degrees and stay in frame. Further left than that is not a placement problem, it is a seat problem.

Set down beside the headset. Not interactive — the era spends its presses on the laptop and the visor; this is the other half of the kit lying where she left it. ⛑ z 0.50 -> 0.10: at 0.50 it stood inside the laptop's own footprint, behind its screen.

⛑ MAYA'S 2026 MACHINE (Sérgio: 'maybe yeah we should have a Laptop in 2026, and that can start as our starting point of interaction for ERA-4 and L will tell us to move to VR'). It sits where the CRT used to, square in front of the seat: the era now OPENS here and is sent from here to the headset. ⛑ yaw 180, and the two wrong answers before it are worth keeping. The model's DEPTH runs along its own z, so at yaw 90/270 the machine faced sideways down the desk and no amount of flipping 90<->270 could ever point it at the seat — I was rotating in the wrong axis and reading each render as if the choice were front-versus-back. Measured: at yaw 0/180 the AABB is 0.246 deep on x by 0.34 wide on z, which is a laptop facing the seat.
